title: Rayon parallel permanent_bipedal3 with chunk-size sweep
description:
Add a rayon parallel implementation of `permanent_bipedal3` that splits the Gray-code subset enumeration across worker threads, with a documented chunk-size sweep on the dev host.

## Background

Ryser's outer loop walks $2^n - 1$ subsets. Parallelising splits the subset range across rayon workers; each worker maintains its own column-sum and combines partial permanents at the end. Chunk-size affects cache locality and load balance: too small wastes scheduler overhead, too large under-utilises workers near the tail.

This issue lands `permanent_bipedal3_parallel` behind the `parallel` Cargo feature (default on per D1c) and documents the chunk-size choice via a microbench in `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/parallel_chunk_sweep-YYYY-MM-DD.csv`.

Per CLAUDE.md, the Gray-code split must be deterministic — same seed and same $n$ produce identical output regardless of thread schedule.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3_parallel(matrix: &Bipedal3Matrix) -> Fp<3>` exists behind the `parallel` feature.
- [ ] [hard] Output bit-identical to `permanent_bipedal3` (T9) on 100 random matrices for each $n \in \{20, 24, 28, 32\}$, regardless of thread count.
- [ ] [hard] CSV at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/parallel_chunk_sweep-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` records throughput vs chunk-size on $n=28$ for chunk sizes spanning 4 orders of magnitude; the chosen default is justified in a comment.
- [ ] [hard] Determinism test: same RNG seed and same $n=24$ produce the same `Fp<3>` output across 10 repeated runs with rayon thread count varied 1, 2, 4, 8, 12.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci --features parallel` passes.
